Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0036", "row_sha256": "293b82cf0f4a2f6ea5a6e91302423aef5d8a5f8122d74b37a24b0d87f3fb2b84", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
can you shape this into a useful prompt for an internal payroll handoff note, not the note itself. it is for the first-half-of-may payroll export at willow bend arts, a small organization with workshop staff and an admin team. this is a made-up example for the note, but please treat the details below as the information it should use. the payroll period is may 1 through may 15, 2025, and the export is prepared in the cedarpay payroll portal. the person preparing this run is lena ortiz, payroll coordinator, and dev shah is the person who reviews the export against the payroll register. don't turn this into a general payroll policy or a guide for every pay period; it needs to stay about this particular handoff and the people and dates here.

we need the note to explain the small sequence of work in plain language, because it gets passed from payroll to finance and a reader may not have made this export before. first lena opens the payroll portal and chooses the may 1 to may 15 pay period, then runs the payroll export report as a csv. the report is saved in the shared folder `Shared/Payroll/2025/May/First`, where the expected file name is `payroll_2025-05-01_2025-05-15.csv`. do not rename files in that shared folder. that instruction is about the files in this folder, not a request to change or describe naming rules elsewhere. it should be easy to see the folder and name in the note, but don't imply that the export has already been reviewed or sent.

please include what the csv contains so finance knows what is being handed over. the listed columns are employee id, department, regular hours, overtime hours, gross pay, tax withholding, net pay, and payment date. workshop staff and admin staff are both included in this export. contractors are not included. don't leave out that distinction or make it sound like contractors are included as a separate category. this is a payroll export, not a report of every person who has worked with willow bend arts. there is a summary row at the end of the csv. keep that fact in the description, since dev uses that row when checking the totals.

there is a check before handoff, and it matters how it is described. dev compares the csv totals with the approved payroll register for the same may 1 through may 15 period. say what is compared, and don't say that the totals match, because the check has not happened in the material here. if the figures differ, dev sends the discrepancy back to lena to look at; the note shouldn't guess why a difference might occur or say the figures were corrected. lena said, "I can check the export after the register is ready, but I won't change the source payroll entries." include that as an ordinary quote, with her name and role clear enough that a reader knows who said it. don't change her statement into a promise that she will alter entries.

maybe put the actual handoff in numbered steps, that feels more usable than a block of prose. something like this but make the order clear: 1) run the export for the right dates and save the csv in the folder; 2) dev checks the summary totals against the approved register; 3) after the check, the export is available to finance for its payroll close work. the last step is a description of what happens after the check, not evidence that it has happened in this example. keep the conditional timing there, because the material doesn't tell us the check is complete. don't add a signoff, approval, or a result.

finance uses the export during its payroll close work to reconcile the payroll amounts with the department records. it is enough to explain that purpose briefly; don't create a new reconciliation procedure or decide which person in finance performs it. the reader needs to understand that the handoff is from payroll to finance, while dev's review is a check before the export is available for that finance work. the note can say the source report is a csv and identify the period again where that avoids confusion, but it shouldn't suggest a second report or another file is part of this process.

there is also a small recordkeeping detail: once the handoff is being recorded, lena may add a date note to the handoff log. this is allowed, and it is separate from the export files in the shared folder. keep it as an ordinary allowed action, not a required step and not permission to edit the csv or the payroll register. the log is called the handoff log; no specific date for the log entry is supplied, so don't fill one in. don't introduce a new folder for the log or give it a file name.

make the final prompt ask for a clear, concise internal handoff note with a practical tone and enough detail for someone in finance to follow the sequence. use short sections or numbered steps if that makes the sequence easier to scan. preserve the names, roles, dates, folder path, exact csv name, listed columns, contractor distinction, quoted sentence, and the condition around the check. avoid making it sound like a completed transaction. finish the note with a distinct factual detail about the handoff log or finance's use of the export, rather than adding a summary or a recommendation. don't add any other operational rules that aren't in these notes.", "output": "Write a clear, concise internal handoff note for the first-half-of-May 2025 payroll export at Willow Bend Arts. The note is for the handoff from payroll to finance and should use a practical tone that a finance reader who has not prepared this export before can follow. Keep it specific to this payroll period and the details below; do not turn it into a general payroll policy or a guide for every pay period.

The payroll period is May 1 through May 15, 2025. The export is prepared in the CedarPay payroll portal by Lena Ortiz, payroll coordinator. Dev Shah reviews the export against the payroll register. Explain the sequence in plain language: Lena selects the correct pay period and runs the payroll export report as a CSV. It is saved in `Shared/Payroll/2025/May/First` with the expected name `payroll_2025-05-01_2025-05-15.csv`. **do not rename files** in that shared folder. Keep this restriction scoped to the files in this folder; do not suggest other naming rules. Do not imply that the export has already been reviewed or sent.

Describe the CSV as containing these columns: employee ID, department, regular hours, overtime hours, gross pay, tax withholding, net pay, and payment date. It includes workshop staff and admin staff; contractors are not included. The CSV has a summary row at the end, which Dev uses when checking the totals. Do not suggest that contractors are included as a separate category or that the export covers every person who has worked with Willow Bend Arts.

Present the handoff in numbered steps if that makes it easier to scan:
1. Lena runs the export for May 1 through May 15 and saves the CSV in the specified folder.
2. Dev compares the CSV totals, using its summary row, with the approved payroll register for the same period.
3. After the check, the export is available to finance for its payroll close work.

Keep the timing conditional: the material does not establish that Dev’s check is complete. Do not state that the totals match, that the export was sent, or that anyone approved or signed off on it. If the figures differ, Dev sends the discrepancy back to Lena to look at. Do not guess why a difference might occur or say the figures were corrected. Include Lena’s statement as an ordinary quote, with her name and role clear: “I can check the export after the register is ready, but I won't change the source payroll entries.” Do not change it into a promise to alter entries.

Explain briefly that finance uses the export during payroll close to reconcile payroll amounts with department records. The handoff is from payroll to finance, and Dev’s review happens before the export is available for that finance work. Do not invent a reconciliation procedure, name a finance staff member, or suggest that a second report or another file is involved.

Include the recordkeeping detail that Lena may add a date note to the handoff log. This is an allowed action, not a required step, and it does not authorize editing the CSV or payroll register. No date for the log entry is supplied, so do not fill one in or invent a folder or file name for the log. End with a distinct factual detail about the handoff log or finance’s use of the export, not a summary or recommendation. Do not add operational rules beyond these details."}]
